answers.answer: Fifty boxes of earth. They were consigned by Varna on the Demeter to Mr. S. F. Billington, Whitby solicitor, and deposited in the old chapel at Carfax. By 1 October the party found that some were missing (Harker: 'There should be fifty of them there, unless any have since been removed'; Van Helsing: 'we have ascertained how many boxes are missing'), so not all fifty were still there.

First mentioned on 26 July 1893 in Mina's journal: Lucy 'has lately taken to her old habit of walking in her sleep' (Mina, entry e0044). Mrs. Westenra asks Mina to lock their door at night. The word 'sleep-walking' is used in the next entries, but the first mention is Mina's.

Only one: Lucy's diary entry of 12 September 1893 (e0106.1). The other eight of her entries (letters of 9 and 24 May, 19 Aug, and diary entries of 23 Aug, 25 Aug, 9 Sep, 17 Sep, plus her memorandum of 17 Sep) mention Arthur.

Four transfusions, in order: (1) Arthur Holmwood, 7 Sept; (2) Dr. Seward (John), 10 Sept; (3) Van Helsing, 13 Sept, implied rather than named: Seward operated and Van Helsing said 'I shall provide' and rolled up his shirt-sleeve; (4) Quincey Morris, 18 Sept.

Garlic grown in the glass-houses of Van Helsing's friend Vanderpool at Haarlem, all the year round; Van Helsing telegraphed for them. Van Helsing arranged them, placing them in Lucy's room himself and making her wreath, with Seward helping to deck the room.
First appears on 5 May 1893 in Jonathan Harker's journal (entry e0004.1), where Harker records that the Slovak and Servian words mean 'were-wolf or vampire'.

One letter, in his own hand, signed 'QUINCEY P. MORRIS': dated 25 May 1893 to the Hon. Arthur Holmwood, inviting him to a camp-fire the next night, with Jack Seward also coming. It is the only passage narrated by or signed by Morris in the store.

experience: The task prompt was the most useful part: it returned a count, and the first grep showed which entries mattered. grep was the workhorse. 'boxes|box' surfaced the fifty-boxes passages with their ids, and 'garlic|Haarlem' pulled the Haarlem line. 'list --source Lucy --by-entry' gave the nine Lucy entries in one call, and grep for Arthur within them settled Q3 quickly. The search command was noisy: for 'boxes of earth' the top hits were mostly unrelated Harker and Mina passages, so I used search only for the first question. Grep's '--by-entry' flag also helped, because whole-entry counts gave a quick sense of where a topic clustered. The 'read' output was clear, and the passage ids were stable enough to cite. 'read' on a bad id (e0107.5) crashed with a KeyError traceback rather than a message. Two things I wish the tool had said: which speaker donated blood on 13 September, which needed a manual read of the surrounding text, and whether a grep match on the 'Morris' name was an author or a mention. The source filter matched only the narrator field, so I had to infer whether Morris had written anything beyond his one letter. A list of all documents signed by a given person would have answered Q7 directly.
